verdictStatement: ACCEPT at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX. Both equality tests the dispatch names pass by ==: quotedNonAuthorityRules is character-equal to live v15's nonAuthority.rules across all four members in order, and fcNonauthTermRequiresVerbatim is character-equal to the live FC-NONAUTH-TERM requires field with all four of its sentences intact. I ran a third quotation check the dispatch did not name — nonAuthorityVerbatim against live nonAuthority.verbatim — and it is equal too. All nine cited path/digest pairs measure equal with zero mismatches, and recordedInputs.HEAD agrees with the top-level head and live HEAD as the artifact's own invariant requires. Every sentence of the live requires field is bound, with the two easiest-to-lose constraints — the Coverage exclusion and the SARIF-not-required clause — each given a dedicated field rather than left buried in a quotation. The prohibited content is genuinely absent, not merely disclaimed: every Coverage occurrence is an exclusion, both G17 occurrences are denials, no bare integer in the file is a D9 or exit value, and the attempted renderer code is expressly left unbound, which is the one place a minted code would naturally have slipped in. The bind attaches to the ACTIVE class and states the INACTIVE sibling's ID-DEP-S2 standing, respecting the CODEX-V3-S1 split in both directions. Four further refutations of my own — a partial bind, a wrong or collapsed class, an overstated predecessor standing, and an implied file-08 status DR-122 does not have — all failed against live bytes.
